dev.tanrei.vocabulary.rationale: One product tells people which keys do what: beside a command in a menu, in a tooltip, in help text and in a list of shortcuts. It shows the keys of the keyboard the person is using, drawn either as keys or as a line of text, and fades the ones whose command is unavailable.

dev.tanrei.llm.usage: Everything a keyboard shortcut reads: for each size, a key cap's minimum height, its padding, its corners and its legend's text style, and the space between the keys of a chord and between the chords of a sequence; the cap's fill, and the edge and deeper bottom edge a layer may give it (the default system draws none); and for each form (keycap, plain) the legend's color, faded when the shortcut is disabled.
rules: Write keys once, in the neutral names (mod+shift+k); the component draws them for the keyboard the person uses (⇧⌘K on Apple platforms, Ctrl+Shift+K elsewhere). Never write ⌘ or Ctrl yourself.
Use mod for the command modifier of a shortcut that exists on every platform; use ctrl only for a shortcut that really uses Control on Apple platforms too.
The keyboard shortcut only shows keys. The product still has to make them work.
Inside a menu, give the item its shortcut; the menu draws it. Do not place a keyboard shortcut in a menu item's trailing text.
container.height is a minimum: a cap grows with enlarged text and with a long legend (Caps Lock).
Restyle through these tokens in a layer; never draw keys by hand.

color.$description: A key cap's fill, in the keycap form (the plain form draws no cap): the faintest fill that still reads as a shape on the surfaces a shortcut sits on, since in the default system it is all there is of the cap. It stays at rest when the shortcut is disabled: the legend fades, the key does not.

height.$description: A key cap's minimum height, per size; also its minimum width, so a single letter sits on a square key. Small sits in a line of body text or a menu row without making the line taller; medium sits with larger text and on its own.

padding-inline.$description: Space on each side of a legend inside its cap, per size. It shows on a legend wider than it is tall (Ctrl, Space, Caps Lock).

shape.$description: A key cap's corners, per size. A key is a small rounded square, not a pill: fully rounded caps would read as chips or buttons (controls are rounded, and a key cap is not one).

color.$description: A key cap's edge and its deeper bottom edge, in the keycap form, where a layer gives them a width; the default system's widths are 0, so it draws neither. Decorative: the legend carries the meaning, so the edge needs no contrast of its own. It stays at rest when the shortcut is disabled.

width.$description: A key cap's edge on its top and sides, drawn inside the cap's size. Nothing in the default system: a cap is a faint fill and no line. A layer that wants outlined keys sets it (sys.border.hairline).

bottom-width.$description: A key cap's bottom edge, drawn inside the cap's size. Nothing in the default system. Where a layer sets it thicker than outline.width it reads as the key's front face; a layer with flat outlined keys sets it to outline.width.

dev.tanrei.vocabulary.rationale: One product may draw its keys flat, as outlined boxes, or with depth, as the keys of the keyboard beside it; the bottom edge is the one measure that tells them apart.

typescale.$description: The legends' and separators' text style, per size.

gap.$description: Space between two keys pressed together, per size: between two caps, or on each side of the separator where the convention has one (Ctrl + K). The plain form draws a chord as one run of text and does not read it.
Space between two chords pressed one after the other (Ctrl+K, then Ctrl+C), per size, in both forms. Wider than a chord's gap, so the sequence reads as two steps.

color.$description: The legends on the caps, and the separators between them: one step quieter than body text, because a shortcut is a hint beside the command, and still text held to 4.5:1 on the cap's fill.
The shortcut drawn as text: quieter than the text beside it, because it is a hint about that text, not part of it.
